newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were steady to 0.50 cents lower, the USDA said in its weekly cash market summary.
Long grain milled rice prices were selling mostly at $20.00 to $20.50 per cwt.; medium grain traded mostly at $18.50 to 19.00; Second heads were steady and brewers were steady to 0.25 cents lower.
Rice by-products were uneven, bran was mostly steady, millfeed was steady to $4.00 higher.
In California, rice prices were steady with medium grain selling mostly from $18.00 to $19.00, second heads were steady, bran was $3.00 to $7.00 lower.
California rice ship loadings: For the week ending May 10, 1997, at the Port of Sacramento there were no rice ship loadings.

Inspections of California rice for export: For the week ending May 10, 1997, there were no rice inspections. The yearly total since October 1, 1996 is 9,476,475 cwt compared to 6,178,783 cwt a year ago.
Feed by-products prices (dollars per short ton, FOB mills).
